Cost of the estimand-aligned (ETI) analysis of a stepped-wedge design

Source: R/stepped_wedge.R
sw_eti_cost.Rd

Variance of the exposure-time-indicator (ETI) estimator of the target (default TATE), the IT variance of the same design, and both relative to the IT variance of the balanced complete wedge with the same number of clusters, periods and covariance.

Usage

sw_eti_cost(
  design,
  phi = NULL,
  icc = NULL,
  cac = 1,
  m = NULL,
  estimator = c("GLS", "TWFE"),
  sizes = NULL,
  target = NULL
)

Arguments

design

numeric vector of length T: cluster counts (or shares) for start periods 2, ..., T, followed by the number wait-listed. The first entry must be positive.

phi

Hussey–Hughes parameter \(\phi = m\rho/(1-\rho)\) (GLS); Inf gives the fixed-effects limit.

icc, cac, m

alternative nested-exchangeable specification: within-period ICC, cluster autocorrelation and individuals per cluster-period (see [sw_phi_nested()]). With sizes, m is not needed.

estimator

"GLS" (default) or "TWFE" (two-way fixed effects, which does not use the covariance).

sizes

optional G x T matrix of cluster-period sizes, one row per cluster in design order (sequence 2 first, wait-list last). Requires integer counts in design and, for GLS, icc and cac.

target

ETI contrast weights (default TATE, 1/L)

Value

list with var_eti, var_it, var_ref (balanced complete wedge, IT, equal sizes at the same covariance; with sizes, the mean size), eti_cost = var_eti / var_ref and it_ratio = var_it / var_ref. Variances are for the stated number of clusters on the covariance scale of the model (GLS: \(V = I + \phi J\); TWFE: i.i.d. unit errors).

Examples

sw_eti_cost(c(6, 6, 6, 6, 0), phi = 2)$eti_cost    # 2.27
#> [1] 2.269942
sw_eti_cost(c(6, 6, 1, 0, 11), phi = 2)$eti_cost   # 1.23
#> [1] 1.227424
